findings: colI_v1.tex l.855-922 (the enumeration behind l.531-546 and l.999-1009) is not exhaustive: a (Gamma_p, l(p))-circle at a non-time-like p with trivial Gamma_p-holonomy (lifted holonomy delta^k, k even) is in none of the printed cases, which assume L hyperbolic (l.794-795) or parabolic (l.797-800). k = 2 is the regular link l(p) (GX.hasType_regular), not a singularity; but k = 4 already gives a singular circle at every p in dS^2 (the 2-fold cover of l(p)) whose unique type is none of the printed ones (GX.exists_hasType_trivialHolonomy_four, from GX.exists_isPositive_delta_four). This is the classification-level form of OQ-128's finding on l.794-795. Smallest correction: exclude trivial Gamma_p-holonomy explicitly ('a singular line of degree k >= 4 with trivial holonomy is a k/2-fold cover of a regular line'), or add the case. Causality (l.1059-1060, degree 0 or 2) excludes them later, so nothing downstream of § 3.6 is affected.

l.1008 ('Recall that the degree is necessarily even') and the proposition's 'degree 2' / 'degree k >= 4': proved that every space-like or light-like type of degree k >= 1 has k even, hence k = 2 or k >= 4 (GX.GammaLinkCircle.HasType.degree_even).

l.1011-1012 ('a cuspidal singular line is actually included in an extreme BTZ-like singular line'), proved in the form: the type at -p of a future cuspidal circle is past extreme BTZ-like and conversely, and LinkType.toLine (sending future cuspidal to the past extreme BTZ-like line, past cuspidal to the future one) is constant on {t, t.antipode} (GX.LinkType.toLine_antipode, GX.GammaLinkCircle.HasType.antipode). Side fact: the time-like future/past and light-like future/past are exchanged, the cone angle, every space-like type, the sign and the degree are kept (the real angle of mirror f^-1 equals that of f, GX.GTilde.angle_mirror_inv).
questions: What is 'the type of a singular line' when its two apices carry different link types (time-like future/past, light-like future/past, cuspidal/extreme BTZ-like)? Reading taken: the line type is LinkType.toLine of either apex's link type, toLine being constant on the antipodal pair; it forgets future/past for time-like and light-like lines, the sign and the cone angle, as the printed list does, and keeps past/future for BTZ-like and extreme BTZ-like lines (the extreme BTZ-like end names the line). l.983-986 say the type is 'the type of the (Gamma_p, l(p))-circle', which is ambiguous at exactly these lines.

Should the trivial-holonomy circles of degree >= 4 be a type of record (they are singular and satisfy the definitions of l.948-953), or should l.948-953 / l.794-800 exclude them? Reading taken: a separate type trivialHolonomy k, outside the printed list.

'The various types are' (l.533): read as a classification (every line has one type, and one only), not as an existence claim. Existence proved only for Misner and for space-like/light-like of every degree 2k with both signs (GX.exists_hasType_listed); that BTZ-like, cuspidal and extreme BTZ-like circles occur is not formalized here. Is existence part of the statement of record?

Misner is one type here; under moved-p isomorphisms it splits in two by chirality (OQ-131 (b)). With the same-p IsIso of OQ-120 (a) the type is an invariant either way. Which notion of isomorphism is of record for 'mutually non isomorphic' (l.785)?

kb_proposals: The type of a (Gamma_p, l(p))-circle is GX.GammaLinkCircle.linkType : GX.LinkType (BBS/HSClassification): read on one oriented lifted pair (GX.PairType), independent of the pair (HasType.pairType), unique (existsUnique_hasType), IsIso-invariant (IsIso.linkType_eq), and at -p it is LinkType.antipode (linkType_antipode).

To compare a statement across lifted developing pairs, read the degree-0 images on i+-(L) (IsLiftedDev.deSitter_degree_zero_iff, bdPlus_/bdMinus_degree_zero_iff): i+-(L) is chart-free, the image is only defined up to Gamma_p.

A 256-case 'two constructors clash' proof: rcases both with Bool patterns (_ | _), dsimp only [the def] at both, then one `first` battery; a branch that rewrites must end in `done`, otherwise it 'succeeds' with the goal open and consumes the hypotheses (seen in pairType_unique).
Inside `first | (obtain … := e h1; …) | skip`, an elaboration error in `e h1` is logged, not caught: guard such alternatives with a helper lemma or an explicit by_cases instead.
angle (mirror f⁻¹) = angle f is GX.GTilde.angle_mirror_inv (through CircleDeg1Lift.tendsto_translation_number₀ and translationNumber_units_inv).
